answer: Each identity registers one dune crest, locks a 70-credit bond, and places a quartz marker photographed into the dune register under its key. A falcon patrol overflies the crest unannounced and records it. The auditor compares patrol image and register; a missing or reused marker burns the bond. The first fee is 29, the kth is 29+6(k-1), the 1000th is 6023, so 1,000 fakes pay 3,026,000 in fees plus 70,000 locked. A rented-marker ring fails because its marker is already registered to another key, exposing reuse. An honest identity pays 29 once and recovers its bond after a clean patrol.
